commits.message:
Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main' into candybar-testing-ihvy.5t2

# Conflicts:
#	src/proc/launch.ts
#	test/proc/launch-group-end.test.ts

refactor(daemon): the lane edge takes its probe last, as productionLaneEdge does; the fake records stdin decoded whole (candybar-testing-ihvy.5t2)

Review round 2 (medium). The daemon's probe comment now says only what is
true: the update watch and the lane edge share it, and the process entry asks
its own before the daemon exists. The spawner fake derived the recorded stdin
chunk by chunk, so a multibyte character split across chunks recorded
differently from what the echo wrote back.

refactor(daemon): one probe feeds the update watch and the lane edge; the next-tick pump lives beside the fake launcher (candybar-testing-ihvy.5t2)

Review round 1 (high). The daemon built its ProcessProbe for the update watch
and let the lane edge build its own, so a fake probe reached only one of them.
The daemon now builds it once and hands it to the lane edge. Two comments that
named the removed pidAlive now name the probe. The duplicated turns() pump
moves next to fakeLauncher.

test: the socket-lease process test reads the real ps again (candybar-testing-ihvy.5t2)

The mass rewrite measured the unit and worker tiers only and swapped this
process-tier file onto the unscripted launcher, which cannot read a start time.

test(proc): real launchers are importable only from the adapter tiers; process.kill from its owners (candybar-testing-ihvy.5t2)

process.kill is allowed in the Spawner, the ProcessProbe and three named
exceptions; a fake is never imported by src; and a test outside the adapter
tiers and a listed exception cannot import the machine's launcher. Each
exception names the ticket that removes it. examples.test scripts its sources.

test: tests that launch nothing hold an unscripted launcher; pending-draw scripts its sources (candybar-testing-ihvy.5t2)

70 test files and three shared helpers imported the machine's launcher without
ever starting a program. They hold a fake with nothing registered now, so a test
that starts to spawn fails loudly and must say what it spawns. pending-draw's
two shell sources are scripted programs on a held clock: no /bin/sh, no sleep.

refactor(daemon): liveness and start-time reads go through a ProcessProbe (candybar-testing-ihvy.5t2)

pidAlive and readStartTime were imported directly by the watchdog, the lease,
the fork-bomb breaker, the lane edge and the update notice. They take a
ProcessProbe now: the system probe is the code that was there, a fake holds the
processes a test names, and one contract runs on both. The watchdog's pidAlive
cases move into that contract.

test(proc): a scripted Spawner, its contract, and the launch policy over it (candybar-testing-ihvy.5t2)

fakeSpawner runs scripted children on the clock it is given; the real launcher
runs unchanged over it, so timeout, abort, output bound, rate limit and the
owner's gate are tested on a held clock with no process. The Spawner contract
runs on the fake (test/unit) and the system spawner (test/integration), and
fakeLauncher registers the lifeline from the launcher's own program constant.

refactor(proc): a launch reaches the OS through a Spawner (candybar-testing-ihvy.5t2)

launch.ts decided every launch and also named node:child_process and
process.kill. The OS side is now a Spawner port (spawn, spawnSync, signalGroup,
groupGone, signalJob) whose real adapter is the moved code, so a test can run
the launch decisions over a child it scripts. jobGroupAlive and endJob become
Launcher members, since they signal through the same seam. Real launchers are
built in system-launcher.ts; child_process lint now allows spawner.ts alone.

fix(bench): the logfmt reader tokenizes, a rotation is told by inode, and the probe click is asked once (candybar-url-handler-uy01.05x)

Medium review of #603. A field spelled inside an earlier quoted value
shadowed the real field, so the reader walks the line's tokens and a
quoted value is consumed whole; it yields every field, so the click
suite reads the problems field without a prefilter that could throw on
a line that only mentions it. A rotated log was told by its size
shrinking, which a busy daemon undoes within the wait; the inode tells
it. A line with no timestamp fails naming the line. The probe click and
its event land once a process, not once a benchmark, and the cold
benchmark's `about` says it quits the live handler app.

fix(bench): the click suite proves the daemon by a round trip, reads the log from the click on, and matches the whole problem (candybar-url-handler-uy01.05x)

Review of #603. A socket file was taken as a live daemon, so a daemon dead
without unlinking ran the bench into a notification on the user's screen;
a stats round trip over the default socket proves it. Each poll read every
log generation from byte 0; the event can only be past where the file
stood at the click, so the read starts there and follows one rotation.
The event match was an unterminated prefix (`-1` matched `-10`); the
problems field is now decoded and compared whole, through one logfmt
field reader beside the encoder, which the daemon world's render reader
shares too (its own read a quoted value's first word). A lost event names
the log searched, since this shell's state dir need not be the daemon's.
The app's name moves beside the scheme so the bench imports nothing of
the installer. Live run: 15 of 15 events found, cold p50 172 ms, warm
99 ms under load 33.

feat(bench): a click's whole time, Launch Services included, is measured for the applet and the forwarder (candybar-url-handler-uy01.05x)

A click suite in the benchmark: open to the daemon's own click event,
cold (handler app quit first) and warm, with the handler that answered
read off the event. Measured on Brandon's Mac: the retired applet
~0.53-0.59 s every click (it exits after each), the forwarder ~0.23 s
cold and ~0.07 s warm. Numbers on the ticket and the epic.

feat(launch): a cut drain or a failed launch pipe shows in the ⚠ indicator (candybar-testing-0x6u.0dh) (#601)

* feat(launch): a cut drain or a failed launch pipe shows in the ⚠ indicator (candybar-testing-0x6u.0dh)

* fix(launch): a held input's failed write is its reader stopping, not a pipe event; the cut's warning is asserted in the cut test, which waits for the holder's end (candybar-testing-0x6u.0dh)

* fix(launch): pipe events stamp on the daemon's clock, share the event hold's answered rule, keep a viewer open across count changes; a pipe-error run is its own outcome (candybar-testing-0x6u.0dh)

* fix(launch): a pipe event carries its own counts, logs itself once, and shows its hold in the draw's facts (candybar-testing-0x6u.0dh)
